title: Forge agent
description: An organization's agent: a Google ADK graph workflow of nodes (ADK agents and other agents, and Forge's workflow steps: approvals, HTTP requests, transforms, filters, delays, If / Switch / Match, loops, for-eachs, merges, ends) joined by edges, run from its start. Every expression (JSONata; in text, inside {{ }}) reads input (the run's), previous (what the node before handed on), steps.<id>.output and .error (the nodes that ran before it), state (the session's) and, in a loop's or for-each's body, its item and index. What each kind hands on is in its config's description.

version.description: Which published version this is; a draft has none (an export of one carries it).

layout.description: Where the builder draws each node, by ID. Runners ignore it.

nodeId.description: Made by the builder, unique in the agent and never reused.

name.description: Its ADK name is this as a Python identifier (Billing specialist: billing_specialist).

outputs.description: The IDs of the ways out of the node, in order: next, or a branching step's (success / error, true / false, a case's or rule's ID and default / otherwise, each / done).

id.description: Made by the builder, unique in the agent: an LLM sub-agent's answer is kept in the session's state under it.
Made by the builder, unique among its agent's tools.

name.description: What it's called: an HTTP tool's or knowledge base's name for the model, as a Python identifier.

source_output.description: One of the source node's outputs.

config_start.description: Where every run starts: what the person or system sends in. Every node reads the run's input, held to input_schema, as input (steps.<start id>.output too).

input_schema.description: A JSON Schema of what a run starts with; {} takes anything.

allow_files.description: Whether a run may start with files: each is saved as an ADK artifact of the run's session, its steps read it there (ctx.load_artifact, an LLM agent's load_artifacts tool), and state.files lists them.

file_types.description: The types of files it takes, by their extension; none takes any type.

start_over.description: When a run stops mid-way (its worker went, a hiccup) and ADK can't carry it on where it stopped, whether it starts over in a new session, every step running again. Off, the run fails and can be resubmitted. A step that fails once the run carried on fails it either way.

config_llm.description: A model works on what comes in with your instruction, and can hand off to its sub-agents. Hands on its answer: JSON held to output_schema when it declares one, else text.

description.description: What it's for: what its parent and peers read when handing off to it.

instruction.description: What it's told to do: a template, where {{ }} puts in the run's data as it runs (input, previous, steps.<id>.output, state, a loop's item). An LLM sub-agent's answer is kept in the session's state under its ID.

model.description: One of the models Forge offers (its model provider configuration's): the provider's key and the model's id. Both empty: the default.

thinking_level.description: How long the model thinks before it answers: the level if the model offers it, else the nearest it does. Empty: the model's own.

output_schema.description: A JSON Schema its answer is held to; {} leaves it free text.

include_contents.description: none: it sees only what it's given, not the conversation so far.

sub_agents.description: The agents it may hand off to.

tools.description: What it can call: the Agents builder's tools (an MCP server, a knowledge base, an HTTP endpoint, an OpenAPI spec, an agent, a workflow), each with that builder's settings.

mode.description: single_turn: it answers once. task: it may ask back until its task is done.

source.description: inline: set up here, with these settings. agent: an agent from the Agents page, used whole (its own instruction, model and tools); the settings above other than output_schema don't apply.

agent.description: The agent from the Agents page (ca_…), when source is agent.

version.description: Which of its versions runs: a published one, its draft, or null for its latest published (as each run starts).

message.description: What it's sent: a template, where {{ }} puts in the run's data; empty sends what the node is handed.

inputs.description: The fields of its input schema (state_schema), each a JSONata expression over the run's data.

config_sequential.description: Runs its sub-agents one after another, each seeing what the last did. Hands on its last sub-agent's answer.

sub_agents.description: Its sub-agents, in the order they run.

config_parallel.description: Runs its sub-agents at the same time, each on its own. Hands on each sub-agent's answer, by the sub-agent's ID: {<id>: answer}.

sub_agents.description: Its sub-agents, in the order they run.

config_loop_agent.description: Runs its sub-agents in order, again and again, up to a number of passes. Hands on the answer of the sub-agent that answered last.

sub_agents.description: Its sub-agents, in the order they run.

max_iterations.description: It stops after this many passes.

config_saved.description: Runs another of the organization's workflows here, whole. Its inputs, when any is filled in, else what comes in, are the other workflow's input (held to its start's input_schema); it hands on that workflow's result: its End's result.

agent.description: Another of the organization's agents, by ID: run here whole.

version.description: Which of its versions runs: a published one, its draft, or null for its latest published (as each run starts).

inputs.description: The fields of its start's input_schema, each a JSONata expression over the run's data. With any filled in, they're its input (an expression that finds nothing leaves its field out); with none, what comes in is.

config_approval.description: The run waits for a person to approve or reject. Hands on {approved, decided_by, comment, decided_at} by its approved or rejected way.

config_human_input.description: Pauses for a person to answer; their answer is what it hands on. Hands on the person's answer, held to response_schema.

message.description: What the person is asked; {{ }} puts in the run's data.

response_schema.description: A JSON Schema of their answer; {} takes anything.

config_http.description: Calls a URL and hands on the response. Hands on {status, headers, body} by its success way, body held to output_schema when it declares one. Its error way hands on nothing; steps.<id>.error is {message, status?, body?, expression?}.

query.description: Query parameters, added to the URL's own: each name and value a template, filled in then percent-encoded. A value that's one {{ }} coming to nothing leaves its parameter out; a list sends it once per item.

body.description: A JSONata expression making the body; an object or list is sent as JSON.

output_schema.description: A JSON Schema of the response's body; {} leaves it undeclared.

credential.description: One of the organization's credentials, by ID: its auth (an API key, a token, OAuth) goes with each request, and only to the URLs it's for. Empty for none.

config_transform.description: Reshapes data with a JSONata expression. Hands on what its expression makes, held to output_schema when it declares one.

expression.description: A JSONata expression: what the step hands on.

output_schema.description: A JSON Schema of what it makes; {} leaves it undeclared.

config_filter.description: Keeps the items of a list its condition holds for. Hands on {count, results}: the items its condition is true for, in order.

items.description: A JSONata expression giving a list.

item_name.description: What the condition calls the item it's on.

condition.description: A JSONata condition, read per item (as item_name, with index); the step hands on {count, results}: the items it's true for, in order.

config_delay.description: Waits a while before going on. Hands on {resumed_at}.

config_if.description: Takes one of two ways, on a condition. Hands on what came into it; steps.<id>.output records the way it took: {branch}.

condition.description: A JSONata expression; true takes the True way.

config_switch.description: Routes on one value: to the case it equals. Hands on what came into it; steps.<id>.output records the way it took: {branch}.

value.description: A JSONata expression; the case it equals (as text) is taken.

config_match.description: Routes to the first rule whose condition holds, or to every one. Hands on what came into it; steps.<id>.output records the way it took: {branch}, or {branches} in mode all.

arms.description: In order: the first rule whose JSONata condition is true is taken (mode first), or every one, at once (mode all).

mode.description: first takes the first rule that holds; all takes every one that holds, at once.

config_loop.description: Runs its body once for each item in a list, collecting what each hands back. Its body (what its each way reaches before coming back to it) runs per item, reading the item as item_name and its place as index; by its done way it hands on {count, results}, results what each item's body handed back.

items.description: A JSONata expression giving a list.

config_for_each.description: Runs its steps once for each item in a list; nothing comes back to it. Its body (what its each way reaches; nothing leads back) runs per item, reading the item as item_name and its place as index; by its done way it hands on {count}.

items.description: A JSONata expression giving a list.

config_merge.description: Waits for the ways coming into it, then goes on as one. Hands on what each way into it handed on, by the step it came from: {<step id>: ...}.

config_end.description: Finishes the run, as succeeded or failed, with a result. Finishes its way with its result: its expression's, or what came in when it has none.

result.description: A JSONata expression giving the workflow's result.

tool_config_mcp.description: A tool: The tools of one of the organization's MCP servers, or one by URL.

server.description: One of the organization's MCP servers, by ID: its URL, headers and sign-in come from there. Empty for one set up by transport, url and headers.

tools.description: The server's tools it may call, comma-separated; empty for all.

tool_config_knowledge_base.description: A tool: Searches the organization's knowledge bases for passages.

knowledge_bases.description: The organization's knowledge bases it searches, by ID: their documents, parsed, chunked and embedded.

description.description: What the model is told it finds there; empty to describe the knowledge bases.

max_results.description: The most passages one search answers.

tool_config_http_tool.description: A tool: Calls an HTTP endpoint with arguments the model fills in.

description.description: What it does: the model decides when to call it by this.

url.description: Where it calls: {name} puts in the model's argument of that name, {{ expression }} one of the run's values. A query parameter that's one argument is left out when the model doesn't send it.

query.description: Query parameters, added to the URL's own: each name and value a template like the URL, filled in then percent-encoded. A value that's one placeholder coming to nothing (an argument the model didn't send) leaves its parameter out; a list sends it once per item.

body.description: Its JSON body (POST, PUT, PATCH), with placeholders as its URL has; one that's a whole value goes in as it is. Empty for none.

parameters.description: A JSON Schema of the arguments: their types and descriptions. The model is offered those the URL and body name.

credential.description: One of the organization's credentials, by ID: its auth (an API key, a token, OAuth) goes with each call, and only to the URLs it's for. Empty for none.

confirm.description: A person confirms each call before it's made.

tool_config_openapi.description: A tool: The operations of an OpenAPI spec, each a tool.

url.description: Where the spec is, when its source is url.

spec.description: An OpenAPI 3 spec, JSON or YAML, when its source is inline.

operations.description: The operations it may call, comma-separated: their tool names (the operationId in snake case) or operation IDs; empty for all.

credential.description: One of the organization's credentials, by ID: its auth goes with each call, and only to the URLs it's for. Empty for none.

tool_config_saved_agent.description: A tool: An agent from the Agents page, called as a tool.

agent.description: Another of the organization's agents, by ID.

tool_config_adk_workflow.description: A tool: Runs another of the organization's workflows and reads its result.

workflow.description: One of the organization's workflows, by ID, called as a tool.

version.description: Which of its versions runs: a published one, its draft, or null for its latest published (as each run starts).

tool_config_code_execution.description: A tool: Runs Python the model writes and reads what it printed.

confirm.description: A person confirms each run, seeing the code, before it runs.

sub_config_llm.description: A sub-agent: A model works on what comes in with your instruction, and can hand off to its sub-agents.

description.description: What it's for: what its parent and peers read when handing off to it.

instruction.description: What it's told to do: a template, where {{ }} puts in the run's data as it runs (input, previous, steps.<id>.output, state, a loop's item). An LLM sub-agent's answer is kept in the session's state under its ID.

model.description: One of the models Forge offers (its model provider configuration's): the provider's key and the model's id. Both empty: the default.

thinking_level.description: How long the model thinks before it answers: the level if the model offers it, else the nearest it does. Empty: the model's own.

output_schema.description: A JSON Schema its answer is held to; {} leaves it free text.

include_contents.description: none: it sees only what it's given, not the conversation so far.

sub_agents.description: The agents it may hand off to.

tools.description: What it can call: the Agents builder's tools (an MCP server, a knowledge base, an HTTP endpoint, an OpenAPI spec, an agent, a workflow), each with that builder's settings.

sub_config_sequential.description: A sub-agent: Runs its sub-agents one after another, each seeing what the last did.

sub_agents.description: Its sub-agents, in the order they run.

sub_config_parallel.description: A sub-agent: Runs its sub-agents at the same time, each on its own.

sub_agents.description: Its sub-agents, in the order they run.

sub_config_loop_agent.description: A sub-agent: Runs its sub-agents in order, again and again, up to a number of passes.

sub_agents.description: Its sub-agents, in the order they run.

max_iterations.description: It stops after this many passes.
